newsitem.title: INDIA: Cotton - Indian prices seen rising on fresh demand.
newsitem.headline: Cotton - Indian prices seen rising on fresh demand.

text.p: Cotton prices have been subdued in the week to Thursday and are expected to gain marginally on fresh mill demand in the next week or two, traders said on Thursday.
They said demand for cotton from yarn mills had been dull due to a downtrend in world yarn prices in the recent past but the trend was reversing in the last few days.
"Prices are likely to firm in the next few days," said a leading cotton trader.
India's political uncertainty, which cast a shadow on its economy in the last three weeks, appears to have blown over.

A new coalition government of the United Front (UF), a 13-party alliance, headed by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral won a parliamentary confidence vote on Monday. The previous UF government lost a confidence vote earlier on April 11.
"Political dust is yet to settle down," said a trader. "A proper government is needed to take decisions on exports and other crucial issues."
Prices remained steady in the week to Thursday as traders adopted a wait-and-watch policy.
Bengal Deshi was steady around 890/950 rupees per maund (37.32 kg). Gujarat Kalyan (medium staple) was unchanged at 13,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
Gujarat Wagad was steady at 12,600 rupees per candy. Gujarat Sankar-4 gained 500 rupees to 16,500/17,000 rupees per candy.
Traders expect prices to come under pressure due to improved arrivals in the near future.
"Prices may fall towards May-end and early-June as pre-monsoon rains could force farmers and merchants to sell stocks kept with them," said a trader.
Traders and farmers sell their stocks on fears that it would get damaged because of the rains and inadequate storing space.
"Once that phase is over, prices may firm again and continue to remain so till the beginning of the new season from October," said another trader.
